ID: `make-interfaces-feel-better`.

## What it does

Checks five areas: typography, surfaces, animations, icons and performance. Compares nested corners, optical alignment, shadows, changing numbers and control feedback with the skill principles. Uses the project’s established style and tests relevant states. A quick review covers the main path with a few findings; full covers the assigned scope more extensively.

## When to use it

Use it when a UI works but some details make it feel inconsistent or awkward. It is a design engineering review of details; it does not redefine product goals, flows or identity.

## How to use it

Ask for it by name, or invoke it with `/make-interfaces-feel-better` in Claude Code or `$make-interfaces-feel-better` in Codex. Name components and states to examine and choose quick or full. Request a before/after comparison with severity, location and consequence. For motion, also test slowed playback and consider only observed defects.

## What it delivers

- Coverage of the five areas
- Findings and concrete replacements
- Rejected candidates, checks and outcome

## Example

Run a quick review of the toolbar: check icon and text alignment, feedback, target sizes and changing numbers.
